title: Ibn al-Nafis
summary: A physician trained at the Nuri Hospital in Damascus, he moved to Egypt in 1236 and became chief of physicians. His commentary on the anatomy of the Canon challenged Galen's view that blood crosses the heart's septum and contains the earliest recorded description of pulmonary circulation. He died in Cairo in 1288.

uncertainty.note: The PMC article gives birth in 1210; Muslim Heritage gives 1213.

where.modern_name: Cairo, Egypt (pinned to the city where he worked as chief physician and died; he was born near Damascus)
where.historical_name: Cairo, Egypt (Mamluk-era Cairo; Baybars reigned 1260-1277 per the PMC article)

importance.justification: Credited by the PMC article with the earliest description of pulmonary circulation, about 300 years before European physicians.

sources.title: Ibn Al-Nafis: Discoverer of the Pulmonary Circulation
sources.publisher: Annals of Saudi Medicine (via PubMed Central)

sources.title: Ibn al-Nafis, the Pulmonary Circulation, and The Islamic Golden Age

reviewer_note: Birth year differs (1210 vs 1213) and the PMC article notes that credit for the discovery has been debated. Link to Ibn Sina rests on his commentary being on the Canon, which the PMC article names as Sharh Tashrih al-Qanun.
